title: Production Deadlock - Two Threads Waiting for Each Other
question: Your production application freezes randomly. Thread dumps show: Thread-1 holds Lock-A, waiting for Lock-B. Thread-2 holds Lock-B, waiting for Lock-A. This is a classic deadlock. Explain: (1) how to reproduce deadlock with code example, (2) how to detect it using thread dumps/jstack, (3) four ways to prevent deadlock (lock ordering, tryLock with timeout, single lock, lock-free algorithms), (4) how to fix this in production without restart. Show code for both the problem and solution.

title: Memory Leak from Lambda Capturing Outer Scope
question: Your application's heap usage grows continuously despite no apparent leaks. Heap dump analysis shows thousands of lambda instances holding references to large objects. Investigation reveals: listeners.add(() -> processData(this.largeDataSet)). The lambda captures 'this', preventing garbage collection. Explain: (1) how lambdas capture outer scope, (2) why this causes memory leaks with listeners, (3) difference between capturing variables vs method references, (4) solutions using weak references, explicit cleanup, or method references. How do you detect this with profilers?
realWorldScenario: Debugging memory leaks from functional code

title: Race Condition in Counter - Lost Updates Problem
question: Your analytics service counts events: counter++. After 1 million events from 10 threads, counter shows 847,293 instead of 1,000,000. This is a race condition from non-atomic increment. Explain: (1) why counter++ is not thread-safe (read-modify-write), (2) show thread interleaving causing lost updates, (3) five solutions: synchronized, AtomicInteger, Lock, semaphore, single-threaded queue. Compare their performance. Which solution for 10 threads? 1000 threads? Provide code for AtomicInteger solution and explain CAS (Compare-And-Swap).

title: ClassCastException from Type Erasure and Raw Types
question: Legacy code uses raw types: List list = new ArrayList(); list.add("string"); list.add(123). New code expects List<String>: List<String> strings = list. At runtime: for(String s : strings) throws ClassCastException when reaching Integer. Explain: (1) type erasure removes generic info at runtime, (2) why raw types break type safety, (3) heap pollution from mixing raw and generic types, (4) how to fix: @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") with validation, or refactor legacy code, (5) detecting this with compiler warnings. Show safe migration strategy.
realWorldScenario: Dealing with legacy code and generics

title: OutOfMemoryError Metaspace - ClassLoader Memory Leak
question: Your application crashes with 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace' after multiple deployments in development. Heap is fine, but metaspace grows with each deployment. This is a classloader leak - old classes not unloaded. Explain: (1) what metaspace stores (class metadata), (2) when classes are unloaded (when classloader is GC'd), (3) common causes: ThreadLocal not cleared, running threads, static references, JDBC drivers, (4) how to diagnose with -XX:+TraceClassLoading/Unloading, (5) solutions: proper cleanup in contextDestroyed, increase metaspace, fix leaks. Show code for ThreadLocal cleanup.
realWorldScenario: Fixing metaspace leaks in web applications

title: Thread Pool Exhaustion - All Threads Blocked
question: Your API stops responding. Monitoring shows all 200 threads are in BLOCKED state waiting for database connections. Connection pool has 20 connections, all in use, but no queries are running. Problem: threads hold DB connections while making blocking HTTP calls to external service. Explain: (1) nested resource deadlock pattern, (2) why thread pool size > connection pool causes this, (3) solutions: separate thread pools for different resources, async processing, timeout on external calls, increase connection pool, (4) monitoring: thread dumps, connection pool metrics. Show code refactoring using CompletableFuture to free DB connections during HTTP calls.
realWorldScenario: Fixing resource exhaustion in high-load systems

title: Reflection Performance Bottleneck in Hot Path
question: Your request latency increased from 50ms to 500ms after adding feature that uses reflection: method.invoke() in a loop processing 1000 items per request. Profiling shows 80% time in reflection calls. Explain: (1) why reflection is slow (security checks, boxing, no JIT optimization), (2) when reflection is acceptable (startup/initialization) vs hot path, (3) solutions: cache Method objects, use MethodHandles, generate code at startup, switch to direct calls if possible, (4) show performance comparison: direct call vs reflection vs cached reflection vs MethodHandle. Provide optimized code using MethodHandle with benchmark results.

title: Parallel Stream Slower Than Sequential - Wrong Use Case
question: You optimized a loop by using parallelStream() expecting speedup on 8-core machine. Performance degraded from 100ms to 300ms. Code: list.parallelStream().map(this::processItem).collect(toList()). processItem() takes 1ms, list has 100 items. Explain: (1) parallel stream overhead (splitting, merging, thread context switching), (2) when parallel is slower: small data, fast operations, shared state, blocking I/O, (3) when parallel helps: large data (10,000+), CPU-intensive ops, (4) ForkJoinPool sizing, (5) measuring with JMH benchmarks. Show calculation: 100 * 1ms = 100ms sequential vs 100ms/8 cores + 200ms overhead = 212ms parallel. Provide decision tree for sequential vs parallel.
realWorldScenario: Choosing between sequential and parallel streams

title: Cannot Create Generic Array - Type Erasure Limitation
question: You want to create: T[] array = new T[10]; but compiler error: 'Cannot create a generic array of T'. You need a generic array in your custom ArrayList implementation. Explain: (1) why generic arrays forbidden (type erasure creates unsafe casts), (2) what happens: new T[10] becomes new Object[10] at runtime, breaks array store checks, (3) workarounds: use ArrayList internally, Object[] with casting, Array.newInstance() with Class<T>, @SuppressWarnings("unchecked") with careful validation, (4) why varargs with generics warning exists. Show safe implementation of generic array-backed container using each approach. Discuss trade-offs.

title: InvalidClassException After Deploying New Version
question: After deployment, your distributed cache throws InvalidClassException: 'local class incompatible: stream classdesc serialVersionUID = 123, local class serialVersionUID = 456'. Old servers serialized User class, new servers can't deserialize. You added a field 'phoneNumber' to User without updating serialVersionUID. Explain: (1) how Java generates default serialVersionUID from class structure, (2) why adding fields changes it, (3) backward compatible changes: add fields with defaults, transient fields vs incompatible: remove fields, change types, (4) solutions: explicit serialVersionUID, versioned classes, use JSON instead, (5) migration strategy: rolling deployment with compatible intermediate version. Show before/after code with proper versioning.
